title: Portable machine profile
description: machine-bootstrap-contract.md §4. A secrets-free, enumerated snapshot of one machine's choices, written by `profile export` and consumed by `profile seed`. The profile is an UNTRUSTED source of interview defaults: it is never configuration to apply, and never an input to any activation or config loader (§4 invariant). Key order here IS the canonical serialization order (§4.1); validated by lib/schema-validate.mjs, whose closed keyword subset means every constraint below is enforced or the schema is rejected. 1.1 (ADR-0048 §2.1) adds the OPTIONAL `statusline_preset` SCALAR — deliberately a bare string, not a field object: §4.6 lets a 1.0 reader ignore an unknown scalar with a warning, while an unknown OBJECT key would refuse the whole document (a nested/custom item shape is exactly the major-bump case §2.1 names). 1.2 adds the OPTIONAL session family — `entry_brief`, `entry_brief_empty`, `session_capture` — as three more trailing scalars, for the same reason and in ALPHABETICAL order: canonicalization emits unknown keys SORTED, so only that order makes a 1.1 reader and a 1.2 reader agree byte-for-byte over one document. Hash alignment is therefore 1.1↔1.2; a 1.0 reader sorts `statusline_preset` in among them and lands on a fourth ordering, which validation and seeding survive but hash identity does not. 1.3 (ADR-0057 §Decision 6) WIDENS the `permissions.claude.defaultMode` enum with `auto` and `dontAsk`. It adds no key, so 1.2↔1.3 hash alignment is preserved. It bumps the minor even though no OLD reader behaves differently for it — §4.6 forgives an unknown KEY from a newer minor and explicitly does not forgive an unknown VALUE of a known key, so a 1.2 reader refuses `auto` whichever minor claims it. The bump buys IDENTITY rather than tolerance: one `$id` must denote exactly one accepted language, or a historical document can no longer be re-validated against the schema that admitted it.

schema.description: Carries a MINOR, not a bare major, because the §4.1 forward-compat rule turns on it: a newer minor forgives unknown scalar keys, a same-or-older minor does not, and an unknown major is refused outright.

boundary.description: §4.3 guard 2. Part of the schema, not an afterthought: the write is refused unless EVERY flag is false — including performs_network_request, not merely the writes_* trio.

hostname_hash.description: §4.2 — a sha256 prefix, NEVER the raw hostname.

observed.description: Per-host and NEVER flattened (§5): a flat map would collapse a Claude/Codex version divergence. Only Codex carries `disabled` — Claude reports no enabled/disabled state (test #31).

model_effort.description: §4.4 — every value is read from USER-GLOBAL config only, so a repository's policy is never exported as another machine's global default. `scope` is always `machine`.

notify.description: §4.0 — `notify_channel` is NOT an egress channel. `telegram` is not a value here and must never become one; egress lives on a separate axis below, precisely so tracked configuration can never activate egress (ADR-0041 §2c).

value.description: §4.1 — a POSITIVE integer string; the existing validator rejects `0`. The profile uses the validator's own accepted form rather than inventing a second encoding.

egress.description: A SEPARATE axis from notify (§4.0). `profile seed` must not map one onto the other. The credential is never here — only its environment-variable NAME and a required boolean (§4.2).

credential_required.description: §4.1 — true ONLY when declined === false AND channel.value !== null. The exact conditional is enforced in code (a schema cannot express a cross-field implication) and tested.

permissions.description: §4.5 — the STORED enum carries whatever each host accepts, unsafe values included, because a source machine's value is shown as a labelled note and must have a field to live in. Safety grading is a present/seed-side rule, not a second schema field.

defaultMode.description: ADR-0057 §Decision 6 — ENUMERATED FROM THE HOST, not from memory: Claude Code 2.1.248 carries the canonical list ["acceptEdits","auto","bypassPermissions","default","dontAsk","plan"] in its own binary, and the omission of `auto` and `dontAsk` made this schema reject a real operator posture exactly as it rejects a nonsense string. Widened IN PLACE rather than at a new minor: measurement showed the reader's forward-compat forgiveness is key-shaped (an unknown KEY at a newer minor is warned and ignored) and does not extend to enum VALUES, `readProfileFile` has no newer-minor fence, and the profile hash is enum-independent — so a 1.3 document carrying `auto` and a 1.2 one produce a byte-identical refusal on an older runtime, and no retained 1.2 profile is reinterpreted (none can contain the new values, which would have been refused at write time).

statusline_preset.description: 1.1 (ADR-0048 §2.1) — the adopted statusline item set, carried as a SCALAR preset id (the six-item owner set is `agentic-6`). Appended LAST and kept a bare string: canonicalization serializes unknown keys after known ones, so a trailing scalar keeps a 1.0 reader's canonical hash aligned with a 1.1 reader's over the same document, and §4.6 lets the 1.0 reader ignore it with a warning. The preset id names a policy; the canonical item-policy definition itself lives with the statusline adapter, never inline here. Optional (absent from required) — a profile exported before the statusline stage carries null or nothing.

entry_brief.description: 1.2 (ADR-0045 §7) — the entry-brief activation posture. A trailing bare SCALAR for the `statusline_preset` reason, and declared with `enum` rather than a loose string for the `notify_channel` reason: a closed set in code is a closed set here, so an out-of-domain value is refused at the write gate and again at the seed gate instead of travelling. USER-SCOPE-ONLY: it activates a session-shaping injected line, so the export reads user-global config only and a seed proposal targets user scope alone — a repo value can never enable it. Declared ALPHABETICALLY with its two siblings, NOT in the config family's own order: canonicalization emits unknown keys sorted, so only this order keeps a 1.1 reader's canonical hash aligned with a 1.2 reader's over the same document. `lib/machine-profile.mjs` PROFILE_SESSION_KEYS carries the same order for the written bytes; the two must not drift.

entry_brief_empty.description: 1.2 (ADR-0045 §7) — how an empty entry brief is reported. Same trailing-scalar carriage, same enum rationale, same user-scope-only rule, and the same alphabetical-order requirement as `entry_brief`.

session_capture.description: 1.2 (ADR-0044 §3) — the session-capture opt-in posture. Same trailing-scalar carriage and enum rationale as its two siblings. NOT user-scope-only: a repo value is legitimate for this key at runtime (it resolves repo → user → default). The export still reads user-global ONLY, per §4.4 — a repo value is this checkout's policy, not the operator default worth carrying to another machine.

provenance.description: §4.4 — every exported value carries USER-GLOBAL provenance, or it is not exportable. A CLOSED set, not free text: these are the three sources the §4.4 readers actually read — the user config.toml (`user-global`), and egress's env / fail-closed-verified local layer, both of which are user-scope by construction. A label outside this set means a reader nobody vetted for the §4.4 rule, and `repo`/`repo-local` must never appear. `null` accompanies a null value (nothing was found to export).

ruleArray.description: §4.1 — capped at 256 entries EACH and sanitized through lib/sanitize.mjs (ADR-0057 §Decision 3 renamed the module when the permission advisor it was named for was removed; the four generic exports are unchanged). A profile exceeding the cap is refused, not truncated: a silently truncated permission list is a security artifact, not a convenience.
